title: F0 configures the existing nested-orchestration substrate; does NOT redesign it
body:
The substrate shipped via `2026-05-02-003-feat-nested-orchestration-v1` already provides parent/child metadata, depth/cycle/signature guards, the `child_charter` parser, the `## Return Condition` parser with the `{satisfied, blocked, superseded}` enum, the `commit_policy` machinery, and the `FAN_IN_MEMO_TEMPLATE` + `pre_resume_after_child:` gate prefix.

F0 ADDS:

- Goal-gap-specific threshold constants (`GOAL_GAP_*`) co-located with `DEFAULT_DEPTH_LIMIT`.
- A private severity-rank table `_GOAL_GAP_SEVERITY_RANK` co-located with the goal-gap constants. **Not in `audit_writer.py`** — that module stays focused on envelope writing.
- Typed Pydantic input structures `GoalGapFinding` + `GoalGapClusterContext`.
- A pure triage classifier function.
- An explicit cap-enforcement helper `validate_goal_gap_child_plan_caps()`.
- A goal-gap child-charter template + builder.
- An evidence path constant + helper.
- A goal-gap fan-in **sibling** parser `parse_goal_gap_fan_in_memo_fields()` (NOT an extension of the existing fan-in parser — touching the generic parser would risk regressing non-goal-gap plans).
- Tests + a reference doc.

**Additive-only invariant (refined wording per amendment at lock turn).** The original wording "only ADDED lines" was too brittle: adding helpers may legitimately require modified lines for `__all__` exports, import re-grouping, or docstring updates. The locked invariant is BEHAVIORAL, not line-by-line:

- no behavior changes to existing public APIs;
- no changes to existing Pydantic model fields;
- no changes to existing guard conditions (depth/cycle/signature);
- no changes to existing return-condition statuses;
- additive helpers / constants / templates / typed structures only, plus `__all__` exports as needed.

Reason: the substrate is sound and was sealed at Plan 003 close-out. Re-opening it for goal-governance reasons risks regressing the anti-recursion guarantees that make the substrate trustworthy. Goal governance is a *use case* for the substrate, not a redesign of it.

How to apply: F001 step 15 + acceptance #16 enforce the amended additive-only invariant via manual diff review + targeted grep, not raw line-count assertions. Any modification of existing public API behavior, Pydantic fields, guard conditions, or return-condition statuses requires re-lock with explicit operator approval.

title: F0 is a prerequisite to F1
body:
F1's pre-impl sufficiency auditor will surface findings of the form 'this should be a child plan rather than a feature' when it walks an objective contract against features.json. Without F0 in place, those findings have no defined target shape — operator improvises charter, return condition, evidence path each time, which is exactly the substrate-vs-policy conflation that produces ad-hoc patches.

Locked sequence per `docs/GOAL_GOVERNANCE_V1.md` §11: F0 (this plan) → F1 → G → F2 → H. F1 lock is blocked on F0 close-out.

Reason: F1's dogfood acceptance (F1.5–F1.7) explicitly requires that the sufficiency auditor identify ≥1 materially correct gap class in Spin & Dine and Glam. Some of those gap classes will likely warrant child-plan recommendations. Without F0 codifying the child-plan shape, the dogfood proof can't actually exercise the gap-triage → child-plan path.

How to apply: F1's plan.md will declare `depends_on: [2026-05-05-002-feat-goal-governance-nested-orchestration-config]` at lock time.

title: Child plan spawning remains explicit / operator-approved — caps are safety rails, not auto-spawn triggers
body:
F0's classifier returns a *recommendation*, not a side effect. The four return values (`inline_fix, child_plan, follow_up_plan, operator_deferred`) tell the operator what the system thinks should happen with the cluster; the operator decides whether to actually invoke the existing nested-orchestration spawn machinery.

The caps in F0 (`GOAL_GAP_MAX_CHILD_PLANS_PER_PARENT_PASS = 3`, `GOAL_GAP_MAX_NESTING_DEPTH = 2`) are refusal points: if the operator tries to spawn a 4th child within one goal-audit pass, the charter builder refuses. Caps prevent runaway spawning, not enable it.

Reason: goal-completion governance is the layer where DontPanic figures out whether a plan satisfied its goal. Auto-spawning child plans against findings would push interpretive decisions (which findings cluster? which clusters warrant a separate plan?) out of the operator's hands and into model behavior — exactly the wrong direction. Operator-approved spawning preserves the human-in-the-loop boundary.

How to apply: F001 step 6 implements the classifier as a pure function returning a Literal type — no spawning side effects. F001 step 9 implements cap enforcement as a refusal (raise ValueError) when the cap is exceeded, not as a silent fallback to follow_up_plan. F001 acceptance #5 tests the cap explicitly.

title: Goal-gap child plans inherit Plan 003 anti-recursion rules (depth, cycle, repeated-finding signature)
body:
Plan `2026-05-02-003-feat-nested-orchestration-v1` codified three anti-recursion guards: (a) depth from the platform `DEFAULT_DEPTH_LIMIT = 3`; (b) cycle by `plan_id` in the parent chain; (c) repeated-finding signature — child can't be spawned to fix the same thing the parent (or any ancestor) was already trying to fix.

Goal-gap child plans are subject to all three guards without exception. F0 does NOT add a goal-gap-specific bypass. The platform depth cap of 3 still binds; F0's `GOAL_GAP_MAX_NESTING_DEPTH = 2` is a tighter goal-governance-specific cap that nests *within* the platform cap (parent → child, no grandchildren without operator override).

Reason: the anti-recursion thesis from Plan 003 ("a child plan is bounded work tied to a named parent finding/objective; depth + cycle + signature together make unbounded chains 'fixing the same thing' impossible") is exactly the property goal governance needs. If F0 carved out a goal-gap exception, it would re-open the failure mode Plan 003 closed.

How to apply: F001 step 14 confirms `git diff` shows zero modifications to the existing depth/cycle/signature guard code. F001 acceptance #6 includes a test that a goal-gap charter past `DEFAULT_DEPTH_LIMIT` is refused; same for cyclic spawn; same for repeated-finding signature collision.

title: Evidence path convention is `evidence/goal-governance/<pass>/...`
body:
Goal-governance evidence is separable from feature-audit evidence in the plan dir to avoid confusing future readers (and the F2 post-impl auditor) about which findings come from which layer.

Locked layout:

```
evidence/
  goal-governance/
    pre_impl/
      sufficiency-findings.json
      objective-contract-walk.json
    post_impl/
      completion-findings.json
      journey-walks/
        <journey>.json      # one file per journey walked
      runtime-evidence/
        <screenshot|log>.<ext>
```

F0 only defines the prefix constant + path-builder helper. F1 writes to `pre_impl/`; F2 writes to `post_impl/`.

Reason: separation of concerns. Feature-audit evidence (pre-existing under `audit/` and `evidence/`) is about implementation correctness. Goal-governance evidence is about objective satisfaction. Mixing them produces the same kind of dispatch ambiguity Plan E just resolved for the validator (gate-state.json being force-validated as Audit envelope).

How to apply: F001 step 4 adds `GOAL_GOVERNANCE_EVIDENCE_PREFIX = 'evidence/goal-governance'` and `goal_governance_evidence_path()` helper. F001 acceptance #7 tests the path-builder produces the documented shape. F1/F2 will use these constants — F0 does NOT pre-create the directories or write to them.

title: `why_child_plan_not_feature` rationale is required on every spawned charter
body:
The most common failure mode for child-plan spawning in goal-governance contexts is reflexive: the auditor flags a cluster, the operator clicks 'spawn child', no one captures *why* this cluster warrants its own plan instead of an inline fix or a follow-up plan in the next iteration. A month later, no one remembers, and the boundary between 'tightly bounded gap' and 'scope creep' has eroded.

Locked: every goal-gap child charter MUST include a `why_child_plan_not_feature` field with non-empty contents (≥20 chars). The charter builder raises `ValueError` if the field is empty or too short.

The 20-char floor is a stub deterrent: 'too big to fix inline' (19 chars) won't pass; 'subscription cancellation flow needs its own state machine + 4 surfaces' will. The point is not enforcing essay quality — it's making the operator articulate enough that future maintainers can reconstruct the decision.

Reason: same logic as the F008 INBOX events requiring structured `reason` fields, or the audit envelope requiring `evidence` on findings. Forcing articulation at decision time prevents the 'why are we even doing this' archeology problem six months later.

How to apply: F001 step 7 implements the builder validation. F001 acceptance #4 tests both the empty-string and short-string rejection cases.

title: No new return-condition statuses beyond the existing `{satisfied, blocked, superseded}` enum
body:
Plan 003's `_LEGAL_STATUSES = {'satisfied', 'blocked', 'superseded'}` covers all three semantically meaningful end-states for a child plan: the child closed its named gap (`satisfied`); the child couldn't close it and is escalating (`blocked`); the child is being voided in favor of a different approach (`superseded`).

F0 reuses these enum values verbatim for goal-gap children. No new statuses like `partially_satisfied` or `redirected_to_follow_up`. If a goal-gap child can't fully close its objective, that's `blocked` (with the reason in the return-condition body) — same as any other child plan.

Reason: enum proliferation is its own failure mode. Every new status doubles the test matrix and creates ambiguity at the parent fan-in step (which states are terminal? which require operator review?). The existing 3 are enough; goal governance doesn't need more.

How to apply: F001 step 8 confirms the existing `_LEGAL_STATUSES` covers goal-gap children without modification. F001 acceptance #9 includes a test fixture exercising a goal-gap return condition through the existing parser, proving no parser changes are needed.

title: Direct-path execution
body:
F0 is mechanical configuration + a pure classifier function + templates + tests + one reference doc. There are no semantic decisions for an auditor to debate:

- Threshold constants come from GOAL_GOVERNANCE_V1.md §6.4 verbatim (operator-locked).
- Classifier rules come from §3.3 + §6.4 verbatim.
- Charter shape comes from §9 Plan F0 deliverables.
- Anti-recursion behavior is inherited from Plan 003 unmodified.
- Evidence path convention is mechanical naming.

A volley would generate findings on style and edge cases; the design surface is already locked. Volley quota is unjustified — same logic as Plans A, C-F001/F002, D, E.

How to apply: `loop_caps.max_iterations: 1` + `agents_required: [claude]` (no auditor needed for direct path). Close-out goes through direct review on the operator's machine. Per the `meta_plan_actions_human_vs_orchestrator` memory: drafting/locking/close-out for direct slices stays human-brokered.

title: Unknown severity is invalid for goal-gap triage and raises ValueError; no silent fallback
body:
Severity values entering goal-gap triage come from auditor envelopes. When an envelope arrives with a severity outside the locked set (`low`, `advisory`, `medium`, `high`, `critical`), F0 must reject it loudly rather than silently treat it as below threshold.

Locked behavior:

- `GoalGapFinding(severity='bogus')` raises `ValueError` at construction time via a Pydantic field validator.
- `build_goal_gap_charter(severity='bogus', ...)` raises `ValueError` at builder time.
- The classifier never has to handle unknown severity at runtime because Pydantic validation rejects it upstream.

Reason: silent downgrade hides malformed auditor output. If a vendor's audit envelope leaks a non-canonical severity (typo, stale enum from an old prompt template, off-by-one mapping bug), goal-gap triage should surface that defect immediately so it can be fixed at the auditor — not absorb the bad value and produce misclassified clusters that look correct.

How to apply: F001 step 6 codifies the Pydantic validator on `GoalGapFinding.severity`. F001 step 9 codifies the builder-time validation. F001 acceptance #5 + #12 lock the rejection behavior with explicit `severity='bogus'` test cases. Same logic applies to any future severity-like field added to goal-gap structures: validate at construction, never fall through silently.

title: Lock signal — F0 plan shape
body:
Locked at 2026-05-05 lock turn. Operator's lock signal:

> 2026-05-05-002-feat-goal-governance-nested-orchestration-config
>
> Status: draft
>
> Single feature is probably enough unless the plan gets bulky:
>
> F001 — Goal-gap triage and child-plan configuration
>
> Acceptance should cover:
> - Defines triage classes: inline_fix, child_plan, follow_up_plan, operator_deferred.
> - Defines child-plan threshold from the decision register: same subsystem AND same journey, >=3 findings, at least one medium+.
> - Adds a child-charter template for goal-gap child plans.
> - Adds return-condition template referencing the parent objective contract.
> - Adds cap rules: max child plans per parent, max depth, max findings per cluster.
> - Requires "why child plan instead of feature" rationale.
> - Defines evidence paths under evidence/goal-governance/.
> - Parent fan-in memo must reference objective contract + child return condition.
> - No runtime spawning automation yet; this is configuration/policy only unless the current nested-orchestration module already has a natural place for constants/templates.
> - No MCP dependency.
> - No OpenClaw dependency.
> - No dashboard work.
>
> Execution path: direct. This is policy/configuration plus tests/docs, not a semantic volley.
>
> Decisions to lock:
> - F0 configures the existing nested orchestration substrate; it does not redesign it.
> - F0 is a prerequisite to F1.
> - Child plan spawning remains explicit/operator-approved.
> - Caps are safety rails, not auto-spawn triggers.
> - Goal-gap child plans inherit Plan 003 anti-recursion rules.

The substrate already has natural places for these constants/templates (`DEFAULT_DEPTH_LIMIT`, `FAN_IN_MEMO_TEMPLATE`, `_RETURN_CONDITION_HEADING_RE`, etc.), so F0 lands additions there rather than introducing a sibling module. This decision keeps the goal-governance config close to the substrate it configures, which matches the locked principle that F0 doesn't redesign.

Any deviation from these terms during F001 implementation requires an explicit D-entry amendment and operator re-confirmation (per the `scope_change_protocol` memory).
